correctness.rationale: Theorem 7.2 of the fresh source gives the exact full-space identity \(P(x_1+\epsilon x_2)=g(x_1)+\epsilon(h(x_1)+dg_{x_1}(x_2))\) for dual quaternionic polynomials. Thus zeros over a fixed primal point are exactly the affine solution set of \(dg_{x_1}(x_2)=-h(x_1)\). The source rank theorem restricts nonempty fiber dimensions to 4, 2, or 0. For \(P_*(x)=x^2+1+\epsilon i\), direct quaternion algebra gives \(dg_J(v)=Jv+vJ\), image \(\mathbb C_J\), and kernel \(\mathbb C_J^\perp\); the lift equation is solvable only at \(J=\pm i\), producing exactly the two displayed affine planes. Their dual parts have real component \(\pm1/2\), so none lies in the quadratic cone.

value.rationale: The fresh source explicitly motivates its new whole-space function class by future study of zeros and factorization of dual quaternionic polynomials. The accepted theorem gives a complete and reusable first structural step: zeros over each primal point are either absent or an affine space determined by the primal differential, with unique lifting at nondegenerate roots. The example \(x^2+1+\epsilon i\) proves that the ambient enlargement is mathematically substantive by producing two entire zero planes disjoint from the classical quadratic cone.
